free_tier.stated: S1 at EUR 5 / month billed monthly, EUR 4.25 / month billed annually: 1 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 30 GB SSD, 2 TB transfer at 1 Gbps shared, 1 IPv4 plus IPv6, DDoS protection included. S2 is EUR 10 / month with 2 vCPU, 4 GB, 60 GB SSD and 3 TB. The page's configuration table header row, one cell per line, reads 'Package', 'vCPU', 'RAM', 'Disk', '1 Gbps', 'Price'.

egress.terms: 2 TB a month included on S1, stated as a column of the plan table; the page also says traffic can be added as an option, without a published rate

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with autoinstall for Hestia CP, VestaCP and Plesk; the page advertises instant setup by email. No API was read.
chaining: The best general-purpose box: 2 GB of RAM, 30 GB of SSD and 2 TB of transfer for EUR 5, with a US east coast, a US west coast, a Moldovan and a Romanian location at one price. It is the node to put a crawler queue, a small database or a scheduler on; the 30 GB disk rules out any archive role.

limits.value: 2 TB a month on a 1 Gbps shared port. The port is shared rather than guaranteed, so a sustained daytime pull competes with neighbours before the 2 TB counter matters, and the 30 GB disk caps any local working set long before either.

notes: The page prints the euro sign; every figure here is spelled EUR to keep the strings ASCII. No free tier was read, so the verdict stays paid-only, but two billing facts on the same page are not a free tier and are recorded here rather than promoted: 'Make an annually order and pay only 10 months', which is two months of service free on an annual term, and a 'FREE TRIAL WINDOWS' note that refers to a 180-day Windows licence trial, not to the server. The vendor's homepage advertises NVMe VPS 'from 6 EUR/mo', so the EUR 5 plan is the SSD line, not the NVMe line. Not in dossier/compute: no record under mivocloud, searched the whole dossier tree. would-settle: whether the 1 Gbps port is per-VPS or per-node, and the price of the traffic add-on.
